title: Catalog item
description: One moment of usable material: a photo, a range of a video, or a framing pulled out of a 360 clip. It is the unit every concept and every build refers to by id. A whole video file is never an item: its usable windows are.

id.description: Unique across the whole project. Convention in schemas/README.md.

path.description: Relative to the project folder, or starting with '~'. Never an absolute path carrying somebody's home directory.

tag.description: Controlled vocabulary: the builders filter on these exact words. 'empty' = nobody in frame.

date.description: Capture date from the metadata, never from the file name or the filesystem.

start_s.description: Required on video and video360: where the usable window starts.

end_s.description: Required on video and video360: where it stops being usable.

duration_s.description: Duration of the whole source file, not of the window.

fps.description: 60 means real slow motion is available.

description.description: What you SAW inside this exact window: what is there, what light, what expression, what moves. Written in English. 'A temple' is not a description.

obstructions.description: Empty or absent means: nothing between the camera and the subject. This is about the RECTANGLE, not about what was happening — the two are judged separately and the second one is the easy one. Measure it, don't guess: `uv run skills/sources/scripts/framecheck.py <file> [--from S --to S]`. When this is not empty, `quality` is at most 2 and `notes` has to say either how a crop removes the obstruction or why the shot is worth it anyway.

hook.description: How much it stops the thumb. 5 is a candidate for the first frame; most material is a 2 or a 3.

subject_present.description: The video's main person is in frame. Counts toward the concept's subject quota.

favorite.description: Starred as a favorite in the library, when the library provides it.

audio.description: What you HEAR in this window and whether it is usable. Empty string if there is none or it is useless.

focus.description: Where the subject sits, 0-1, so a horizontal source can be cropped to 9:16 without beheading anyone.

direction.description: video360 only: the framing this item is. Two items of the same clip closer than 90 degrees in yaw read as the same shot repeated.

sheet.description: Which contact sheet or frame strip this was read off, with its number: 'workspace/sheets/day-03/sheet-01.jpg#14'. This is what makes the catalog auditable.

notes.description: What whoever builds needs to know so they do not get it wrong.

use.description: false + reason for everything dropped. Nothing is ever deleted.

live.description: A photo that is a Live Photo: its ~1.5-3 s movie, measured by skills/sources/scripts/live.py (scan → export → analyze --apply). When `usable` is true the photo is used as a CLIP inside [start_s, end_s], landing on the still with the engine's `tail: "still"` — a still with a push is what you use only when there is no usable movement.

still_s.description: where the sharp still sits in the movie

batch.description: What one context agent writes: workspace/catalog/catalog-<batch>.json. The merged workspace/catalog/catalog.json has the same shape, with batch set to 'merged'.
The batch id this agent owned. One agent, one batch, one file.

agent.description: Which agent wrote it: photo-curator, clip-analyst, 360-scout.

generated.description: ISO date the file was written.

summary.description: Two or three lines on what is in this batch.

struck_me.description: The three things that struck you most. This is the raw material the concepts get written from.

gaps.description: What you could not cover and why.

obstruction.description: What stands BETWEEN the camera and the thing this shot is about. glass: shot through a window or a screen. frame: a mullion, a bar or a door jamb cutting the picture. foreground_people: bodies or heads near the lens who are not the subject, facing any way. foreground_object: a seat back, a pole, a railing, a hand. dirt: specks or smears on the glass or the lens. reflection: the interior mirrored on the glass.
